summary: Iter57 — Full validation of the 3-part 'unique-look-per-template + mode toggle + Maison Verde bug fixes' pass. All 17 backend regression tests in test_iter57_looks.py pass (100%): all 7 canonical tenants carry the expected per-template theme fingerprints (site_niche/mode/font_heading/site_preset), the 7 themes are pairwise distinct on (primary,bg,font_heading,site_preset,radius), POST /apps/{id}/templates/{key}/apply against a throwaway tenant maps 4/4 tested keys (retail→editoriallux+Cormorant Garamond, fitness→energy+Syne, finance→ledger+Lora, logistics→freight+Barlow Condensed), PUT /apps/{id}/theme persists a subsequent mode + manual primary override, client.editor sees exactly 1 tenant (Northwind), admin sees 7, and public /api/public/showcase + /api/public/landing/tenants both return live data. Frontend computed-CSS checks against the live public preview URLs confirmed: Maison Verde (light) renders on cream #FBF8F1 with Cormorant Garamond, h1 rgb(17,17,17), h2/p rgb(51,51,51), a visible 'Find a store' secondary CTA with 2px dark border + dark label, container class `min-h-screen dsv2 tmode-light pr-site-editoriallux`, zero strikethroughs. Northwind (dark) → Oswald + white heading + rgb(229,229,229) body. Northline (dark) → Barlow Condensed. Forge (dark) → Syne + black bg. Nocturne (dark) → tmode-dark pr-site-noir + Syne + purple #A855F7 accent + a 'Take the virtual tour' cta2 with light 2px outline + white label. Backend startup log confirms retheme_all + ensure_demo_tenants + ensure_editor_tenant all fire correctly. IMPORTANT: The preview_token URLs listed in the review request are stale for 6 of the 7 tenants — during my run the demo tenants were wiped once and ensure_demo_tenants regenerated fresh preview_token values (only Maison Verde's token pv_62958c58ce0422a1a58b matches). Any external caller reusing the review's URLs (except Maison Verde and Northwind) will get 'Preview link is invalid or has been revoked' — because the token is stored on the tenant doc and rotates on every demo-restore.

minor.issue: preview_token is generated fresh (_id('pv')+uuid.uuid4().hex[:8]) every time a demo tenant is re-inserted, so any preview URL previously published (docs, release notes, review requests) breaks the moment the DB is rolled back and the demo re-inserts run. Suggest deriving preview_token deterministically from app_id (e.g. 'pv_' + hashlib.md5(app_id.encode()).hexdigest()[:20]) so the six documented public preview links remain stable across resets.

Between the pytest run (12:48) and a follow-up admin API check (12:52) 6 of 7 tenants disappeared without an intentional delete — the only mutation my suite performed was creating and DELETE'ing one throwaway tenant. supervisorctl restart backend triggered ensure_demo_tenants to restore 5/6 demo tenants + ensure_editor_tenant restored Northwind, so the self-healing works. Root cause of the mid-session wipe is unclear (this is the same 'rollback earlier today' the review context flagged); recommend adding a lifecycle audit log or a scheduled consistency check that logs a WARNING when a DEMO_TENANTS or EDITOR_TENANT_ID row goes missing without a DELETE audit event.

action_items: Make preview_token deterministic per app_id in seed_sites.ensure_demo_tenants so publicly-shared preview URLs survive DB rollbacks (Maison Verde still works because its token happened to be regenerated to the documented value or was never rotated; the other five are all rotated on re-seed).
Optional: add a startup consistency check that WARNs when the canonical DEMO_TENANTS or EDITOR_TENANT_ID vanish, so silent rollbacks are visible in the logs.
critical_code_review_comments: site_content.LOOKS is well-designed — every one of 16 entries carries a genuinely distinct (primary, bg, font_heading, site_preset, radius) combination and mode is intentionally set per-niche (retail/legal/education/real_estate/healthcare = light, everything else = dark). retheme_all() correctly gates on look_v so tenants that already carry LOOK_V=1 are skipped, avoiding thrash on every restart.

templates.apply_template correctly maps template key → LOOKS niche via INDUSTRY_MAP with a fallback path when key isn't in LOOKS. Verified retail/fitness/finance/logistics map to their unique visual identities on a throwaway tenant. site_niche is persisted on the app so subsequent renders continue to pick the same look.

studio.put_theme's ThemeIn model wraps the payload as {'theme': {...}} rather than accepting the theme dict at the top level. Fine but worth documenting — the review request implied a top-level payload, and my first attempt returned 422 until I wrapped it.
POST /api/apps requires 'industry' as a required field (Pydantic 422 otherwise). Not a bug, but worth noting for anyone testing throwaway tenant creation.
seed_sites.ensure_demo_tenants inserts a fresh preview_token on every re-seed. Deterministic tokens (hash of app_id) would make the published preview URLs survive rollbacks.
Legacy /app/backend/tests/test_iter{11..52}*.py suites still hardcode long-dead tenant ids — per the review agent-to-agent context they are legacy and left alone.

context_for_next_testing_agent: The 3-part iter57 delivery (unique-look-per-template + Site Mode toggle + Maison Verde Part-3 bug fixes) is functionally correct and reproducible. Live preview URLs listed in the review request are stale for 5 tenants (Meridian, Nocturne, Orbit, Forge, Northline) because ensure_demo_tenants rotates preview_token on every re-seed — fetch the current tokens dynamically via `curl -b cj $API/api/apps | jq '.[] | {name, preview_token}'` before running preview-URL tests. rca of the issue: No functional regression in the iter57 delivery itself. Two operational observations: (1) preview_token is non-deterministic across re-seeds, so publishing a preview URL is a one-shot commitment — remediation is deterministic token derivation from app_id in ensure_demo_tenants. (2) A silent tenant wipe occurred mid-session (same class of event flagged in the review context 'a past pass wiped real tenants and 5 demo tenants were lost again to a rollback earlier today'); the self-healing ensure_demo_tenants + ensure_editor_tenant on the next backend restart fully restored 6/7 tenants (plus the persistent Maison Verde), which validates the iter55/56 idempotency fixes — but the source of the mid-session delete remains untraced. Suggest wrapping DELETE /api/apps/{app_id} in a startup-check audit log so future silent wipes surface immediately.
